summary: Jacob marries Bilhah, and she bears Dan and Naphtali—He marries Zilpah, and she bears Gad and Asher—Leah bears Issachar and Zebulun and a daughter, Dinah—Then Rachel conceives and bears Joseph—Jacob works for Laban for wages of cattle and sheep.
meta_description: Jacob marries Bilhah, and she bears Dan and Naphtali—He marries Zilpah, and she bears Gad and Asher—Leah bears Issachar and Zebulun and a daughter, Dinah—Then Rachel conceives and bears Joseph—Jacob works for Laban for wages of cattle and sheep.

footnotes.note3_a: HEB be built up by her (Gen. 16:2).
footnotes.note6_a: IE He has judged, or vindicated. Gen. 49:16 (16–18); 1 Chr. 2:2.
footnotes.note8_a: HEB The wrestlings of God have I wrestled with my sister.
footnotes.note11_b: IE Good fortune (wordplay on the Hebrew words gedud, “troop,” and gad, “fortune”).
footnotes.note18_b: IE (perhaps) There is a recompense. Gen. 49:14 (14–15).
footnotes.note20_b: The Hebrew zevul means “exalted abode”; see in Isa. 63:15. Gen. 49:13; 2 Ne. 19:1.
footnotes.note24_a: “Joseph” relates both to the Hebrew root yasaph, “to add,” and to asaph, meaning both “to take away” and “to gather.” The context plays upon all of these meanings. TG Israel, Joseph, People of.
footnotes.note32_a: HEB sheep. “Cattle” is older English for “flock” or “herd” as part of one’s property, or “stock.” Enos 1:21; Ether 9:18; Abr. 5:21.
